bioLeak — rules for working on this package

Source: CLAUDE.md

bioLeak executes leakage-safe resampling, train-only preprocessing (guards), leakage audits and randomization inference. Its sibling package ../splitGraph declares dataset dependency structure and emits a split_spec; bioLeak consumes it through as_leaksplits().

Open defects found in review live in dev/OPEN-ISSUES.md. Read it before touching delta_lsi.R, guards.R, make_split_plan.R or splitgraph_adapter.R, and update it when an issue is fixed or found.

1. Package boundary

  • Fold execution, guards, audits and inference belong here. Graph modelling, dependency derivation and leakage declaration belong in splitGraph.
  • Do not make splitGraph a hard dependency. It stays in Suggests; every use is behind requireNamespace("splitGraph", quietly = TRUE) or skip_if_not_installed("splitGraph").
  • A new Imports entry needs the user’s approval. Prefer Suggests plus a runtime check.

2. What “done” means

A milestone or fix is done only when all of these hold. Until then, call it “implemented, unverified”, never “completed”.

  1. Unit tests cover the case where the feature must act, the case where it must not act, and at least one edge case (empty, single group, NA, unseen level).
  2. The relevant probe in .claude/skills/verify-change/probes/ passes, or a new probe was added for behaviour the probes don’t yet cover.
  3. NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e 'devtools::test()' reports 0 failures and no new skips.
  4. Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise()' leaves no diff in man/ or NAMESPACE. Never hand-edit man/*.Rd or NAMESPACE.
  5. NEWS.md has an entry under the development version. Behaviour changes that can alter results go under “Bug fixes (results can change)” or a “Breaking changes” heading.
  6. The change is committed. Uncommitted work is not done, whatever a roadmap says.

Iterative checking (required)

Verification runs in rounds, as defined in the verify-change skill: R1 claim-vs-diff review → R2 tests + probes → R3 adversarial probes (null calibration, benign look-alikes, unseen levels, edge cases) → R4 independent review by a fresh subagent given the code, not the conclusions. Any finding is fixed, then every round is re-run from R2, because fixes break other things. Stop only after a full round finds nothing new. After three fix cycles that still find new defects, stop and report to the user instead of continuing. Each round’s result goes in the report; a round is never skipped silently.

3. Statistical rules (these caused real defects; do not relax them)

  • Inference units must be independent. Never assign one fold-level statistic to several units (groups, batches, cells) and then treat them as exchangeable. R_eff and every n_units must equal the number of independent units. If a per-unit statistic is needed, compute it from that unit’s own predictions.
  • Every new or changed p-value needs a null calibration check: simulate under H0, require type-I error ≤ α + 3·sqrt(α(1−α)/B). Add a power sanity check under a clear alternative. Correct-looking code has shipped at 59% type-I error at α = 0.05.
  • No silent no-ops. A learned transform must define what happens on levels unseen in training (batch, factor level, column). It either errors or warns and applies a documented fallback. The same holds for any algorithm that cannot reach its target: say so.
  • Train-only means train-only. A guard’s transform() output for a row must not depend on other test rows. Fitted state comes only from training rows, and its hash must change when the configuration changes.
  • Removing a group effect can remove biology. Batch/location-scale adjustment must accept protected covariates, or warn when the batch is associated with the outcome in the training fold.
  • Diagnostics need both error directions tested: one fixture that must be flagged, and one benign look-alike that must not be flagged.
  • Method names must match the method. Don’t call something “ComBat” unless it implements ComBat’s model; document deviations in @details.

4. The splitGraph ↔︎ bioLeak seam

  • Fields read from split_spec: sample_data (sample_id, group_id, batch_group, study_group, site_group, region_group, platform_group, assay_group, timepoint_id, order_rank, stratum), group_var, block_vars, time_var, stratum_var, ordering_required, constraint_mode, constraint_strategy.
  • Reading a new field, or changing how one is interpreted, means:
    1. update splitGraph’s tests/testthat/test-bioleak-contract.R and ?as_split_spec (“What downstream consumers read”);
    2. check whether splitGraph’s .depgraph_schema_version must bump (rules in ../splitGraph/dev/release.md §1);
    3. run the contract-check skill.
  • Contract tests use skip_if_not_installed(), which sees the installed copy, not the working tree. Install both development versions before trusting a contract test result (the contract-check skill does this).

5. Commands

NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'                     # full suite
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "delta-lsi")'               # one file
Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise()'                             # docs + NAMESPACE
Rscript .claude/skills/verify-change/probes/inference_calibration.R
Rscript .claude/skills/verify-change/probes/guard_invariants.R
R CMD build . && R CMD check --as-cran bioLeak_<ver>.tar.gz     # before release

Run probes from the package root. They exit non-zero when any FAIL line is printed.

6. Working conventions

  • Fix bugs test-first: write the failing test or probe, see it fail, then fix.
  • Keep internal helpers dot-prefixed (.dlsi_*, .guard_*, .bio_*). Raise conditions through .bio_stop() / .bio_warn() with a condition class.
  • Never change set.seed() behaviour of user-visible functions without a NEWS entry. New internal code that needs randomness saves and restores .Random.seed instead of leaving the user’s global RNG state changed.
  • Commit or push only when the user asks. This repo often carries large uncommitted work; never git checkout, reset or stash it away.
